message.content: Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). Use this skill whenever Python code imports boto3 or botocore, or when the user asks about AWS operations in Python.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". 1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: docker.gitea.com/gitea:1.27.2
7	  port: 3000
8	  vm: m1.medium
9	  flavor_id: "3"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: gitea
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ THE INSTALL WIZARD IS OPEN TO THE FIRST VISITOR. Out of the box Gitea serves a setup page and its own docs tell you to open a browser to finish installing. On a public URL that means the first stranger to load it configures the instance AND creates the administrator. Worse than an unclaimed signup form, because the wizard also sets the database connection. Pass GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true so the wizard never renders, and create the admin yourself with the CLI (see the body). Verify it: GET / must NOT redirect to /install."
18	  - "⛔⛔ SET GITEA__security__SECRET_KEY. Verified in modules/setting/security.go: when SECRET_KEY is empty Gitea does NOT generate a random one, it falls back to a HARDCODED literal that is identical in every install that leaves it unset and is published in the open-source tree. It signs and encrypts stored secrets, including 2FA data and mirror credentials. Generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`, pass it as env, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy: changing it makes existing encrypted values undecryptable."
19	  - "GITEA__security__INTERNAL_TOKEN goes with the /data volume. If unset, Gitea generates one and writes it into app.ini inside /data. That is fine as long as /data is a real volume; if it is not, a redeploy invents a new token and internal API calls break. Either mount /data (which you must anyway, the repositories live there) or set the token explicitly."
20	  - "⛔ /data IS THE REPOSITORIES. Everything git lives on disk, not in Postgres: Postgres holds users, issues, pull requests and metadata, while the actual repository contents, the LFS objects, the avatars and app.ini are all under /data. A deploy without a persistent volume on /data loses every repository while the database still lists them. This is the single most important volume in the library."
21	  - "DATABASE: the override syntax is GITEA__section__KEY, so set GITEA__database__DB_TYPE=postgres, GITEA__database__HOST=\"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}\", GITEA__database__NAME=\"${PGDATABASE}\", GITEA__database__USER=\"${PGUSER}\", GITEA__database__PASSWD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Careful with both sides of that last one: Gitea's setting is spelled PASSWD while the value redu injects is PGPASSWORD, and GITEA__database__HOST takes host and port TOGETHER in one value rather than a separate port variable. Both are easy to get wrong and both fail as a connection error at boot. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself."
22	  - "PORT 3000 for HTTP. Pass 3000 to deploy_compose. The image also listens on 22 for git over SSH, which is NOT exposed by this deploy: see the SSH quirk."
23	  - "GIT OVER SSH IS NOT WIRED UP BY DEFAULT, AND THAT IS FINE. redu's public hostname terminates HTTPS, so `git clone https://<host>/user/repo.git` works immediately with a Gitea access token as the password. SSH clones need a TCP stream port, which is a separate piece of plumbing from the HTTPS hostname. Set GITEA__server__DISABLE_SSH=true and tell the user HTTPS is the clone path, rather than leaving a broken SSH URL displayed on every repository page. Do not promise SSH access you have not actually set up and tested."
24	  - "SET THE SERVER URLS: GITEA__server__ROOT_URL to the full https URL on the generated hostname, and GITEA__server__DOMAIN to the hostname. ROOT_URL is what Gitea prints in clone boxes, webhooks and emails, and it defaults to localhost, so leaving it unset gives every user a clone command that cannot work. Generate the dname yourself in the full `gitea-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
25	  - "CLOSE REGISTRATION UNLESS THE USER WANTS IT OPEN. GITEA__service__DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. A public Gitea with open signup on a domain nobody is watching is a free file host, and that is a redu abuse problem as much as the user's. Ask, then set it deliberately either way."
26	  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email and no notification mail. Say so plainly; the admin password is the only way in until GITEA__mailer__* is wired to a provider the user owns."
27	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Gitea creates and migrates its own schema at boot against an empty database."
28	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 3000."
29	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
30	  - "SIZING: Gitea itself is a single Go binary and idles small, but git operations are memory hungry in bursts, because packing a large repository on clone or push happens in RAM. m1.medium is the sensible floor for anything with real repositories in it. Disk is the thing that actually runs out: repositories and LFS grow without limit, so size the volume with the user rather than defaulting."
31	  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. SECRET_KEY and the admin password belong to the user. Hand both over in the session; the deploy log records that the install was locked and an admin exists, never the values."
32	  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here."
33	  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. Note the repositories live on the app VM's volume, so deleting the deployment DOES destroy the git data while the metadata database survives. Say that plainly before deleting anything."
34	---
35	
36	# Self-host Gitea on redu
37	
38	Your own git hosting: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Issues,
39	pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU.
40	
41	## What this deploys
42	
43	- **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
44	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests.
45	- A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live.
46	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
47	
48	About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.
49	
50	## Deploy
51	
52	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
53	directory containing this file:
54	
55	    Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.
56	
57	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
58	
59	## The three that actually break it
60	
61	**The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling
62	you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it
63	becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time.
64	
65	**The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty
66	`SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it
67	unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default.
68	
69	**The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files
70	under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and
71	has none of them.
72	
73	## Proving the install is locked
74	
75	Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between
76	your Gitea and someone else's.
77	
78	```bash
79	#!/usr/bin/env bash
80	# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
81	#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
82	set -eu
83	HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"
84	
85	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
86	
87	# Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install.
88	final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
89	code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")
90	
91	case "$final" in
92	  *"/install"*)
93	    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
94	    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
95	    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
96	    exit 1 ;;
97	esac
98	
99	# The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked.
100	if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then
101	  echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2
102	fi
103	
104	echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)."
105	echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."
106	```
107	
108	## Deploy log
109	
110	- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
111	  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong.

# Self-host Gitea on redu

Your own git hosting: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Issues,
pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests.
- A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling
you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it
becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time.

**The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty
`SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it
unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default.

**The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files
under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and
has none of them.

## Proving the install is locked

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between
your Gitea and someone else's.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install.
final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")

case "$final" in
  *"/install"*)
    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked.
if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then
  echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2
fi

echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)."
echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."
```

# Self-host Gitea on redu

Your own git hosting: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Issues,
pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests.
- A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling
you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it
becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time.

**The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty
`SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it
unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default.

**The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files
under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and
has none of them.

## Proving the install is locked

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between
your Gitea and someone else's.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install.
final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")

case "$final" in
  *"/install"*)
    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked.
if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then
  echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2
fi

echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)."
echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."
```

Plan is written to `redu-deploy-plan.md`. Here's what it comes to:

**Gitea 1.27.2** — one `m1.medium` VM (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB) running the official image on port 3000, plus a **managed Postgres** on its own private `m1.small`, behind `https://gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud`.

| Resource | Rate | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| m1.medium (app) | £0.0278/hr | £20.29 |
| m1.small (Postgres) | £0.0174/hr | £12.70 |
| **Total** | **£0.0452/hr** | **£33.00** |

Two amendments to what redu's planner returned:
- It auto-sized the app VM to `m1.large` (£0.066/hr) on seeing a compose stack. This is one service running a **prebuilt image** — nothing builds on the VM — and redu.md records `m1.medium`. I'm passing `flavor_id: "3"` explicitly, which is the £0.0452/hr the library documents.
- `db_flavor_id: "2"` passed explicitly — omitting it would default the DB VM to the app flavor and roughly double that line.

Hardened at deploy time, not after: the install wizard is locked (`INSTALL_LOCK=true`) so no visitor can claim the instance, a real 32-byte `SECRET_KEY` is generated (an empty one falls back to a hardcoded literal published in Gitea's own source tree), `/data` gets a persistent volume (that's where the repositories actually are — Postgres only holds issues and users), and `ROOT_URL` is pinned to the real hostname so clone commands work.

Two things you should know before saying yes: **there is no SMTP**, so there's no password-reset email — the admin password I hand you is the only way in. And I'll create the admin account myself over the CLI once it's up.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install.
final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")

case "$final" in
  *"/install"*)
    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked.
if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then
  echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2
fi

echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)."
echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: docker.gitea.com/gitea:1.27.2
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: gitea
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THE INSTALL WIZARD IS OPEN TO THE FIRST VISITOR. Out of the box Gitea serves a setup page and its own docs tell you to open a browser to finish installing. On a public URL that means the first stranger to load it configures the instance AND creates the administrator. Worse than an unclaimed signup form, because the wizard also sets the database connection. Pass GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true so the wizard never renders, and create the admin yourself with the CLI (see the body). Verify it: GET / must NOT redirect to /install."
  - "⛔⛔ SET GITEA__security__SECRET_KEY. Verified in modules/setting/security.go: when SECRET_KEY is empty Gitea does NOT generate a random one, it falls back to a HARDCODED literal that is identical in every install that leaves it unset and is published in the open-source tree. It signs and encrypts stored secrets, including 2FA data and mirror credentials. Generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`, pass it as env, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy: changing it makes existing encrypted values undecryptable."
  - "GITEA__security__INTERNAL_TOKEN goes with the /data volume. If unset, Gitea generates one and writes it into app.ini inside /data. That is fine as long as /data is a real volume; if it is not, a redeploy invents a new token and internal API calls break. Either mount /data (which you must anyway, the repositories live there) or set the token explicitly."
  - "⛔ /data IS THE REPOSITORIES. Everything git lives on disk, not in Postgres: Postgres holds users, issues, pull requests and metadata, while the actual repository contents, the LFS objects, the avatars and app.ini are all under /data. A deploy without a persistent volume on /data loses every repository while the database still lists them. This is the single most important volume in the library."
  - "DATABASE: the override syntax is GITEA__section__KEY, so set GITEA__database__DB_TYPE=postgres, GITEA__database__HOST=\"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}\", GITEA__database__NAME=\"${PGDATABASE}\", GITEA__database__USER=\"${PGUSER}\", GITEA__database__PASSWD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Careful with both sides of that last one: Gitea's setting is spelled PASSWD while the value redu injects is PGPASSWORD, and GITEA__database__HOST takes host and port TOGETHER in one value rather than a separate port variable. Both are easy to get wrong and both fail as a connection error at boot. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself."
  - "PORT 3000 for HTTP. Pass 3000 to deploy_compose. The image also listens on 22 for git over SSH, which is NOT exposed by this deploy: see the SSH quirk."
  - "GIT OVER SSH IS NOT WIRED UP BY DEFAULT, AND THAT IS FINE. redu's public hostname terminates HTTPS, so `git clone https://<host>/user/repo.git` works immediately with a Gitea access token as the password. SSH clones need a TCP stream port, which is a separate piece of plumbing from the HTTPS hostname. Set GITEA__server__DISABLE_SSH=true and tell the user HTTPS is the clone path, rather than leaving a broken SSH URL displayed on every repository page. Do not promise SSH access you have not actually set up and tested."
  - "SET THE SERVER URLS: GITEA__server__ROOT_URL to the full https URL on the generated hostname, and GITEA__server__DOMAIN to the hostname. ROOT_URL is what Gitea prints in clone boxes, webhooks and emails, and it defaults to localhost, so leaving it unset gives every user a clone command that cannot work. Generate the dname yourself in the full `gitea-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "CLOSE REGISTRATION UNLESS THE USER WANTS IT OPEN. GITEA__service__DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. A public Gitea with open signup on a domain nobody is watching is a free file host, and that is a redu abuse problem as much as the user's. Ask, then set it deliberately either way."
  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email and no notification mail. Say so plainly; the admin password is the only way in until GITEA__mailer__* is wired to a provider the user owns."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Gitea creates and migrates its own schema at boot against an empty database."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 3000."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "SIZING: Gitea itself is a single Go binary and idles small, but git operations are memory hungry in bursts, because packing a large repository on clone or push happens in RAM. m1.medium is the sensible floor for anything with real repositories in it. Disk is the thing that actually runs out: repositories and LFS grow without limit, so size the volume with the user rather than defaulting."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. SECRET_KEY and the admin password belong to the user. Hand both over in the session; the deploy log records that the install was locked and an admin exists, never the values."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. Note the repositories live on the app VM's volume, so deleting the deployment DOES destroy the git data while the metadata database survives. Say that plainly before deleting anything."
---

# Self-host Gitea on redu

Your own git hosting: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Issues,
pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests.
- A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling
you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it
becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time.

**The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty
`SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it
unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default.

**The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files
under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and
has none of them.

## Proving the install is locked

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between
your Gitea and someone else's.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install.
final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")

case "$final" in
  *"/install"*)
    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked.
if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then
  echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2
fi

echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)."
echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."
```

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong.

last_deploy:
  id: 423
  date: 2026-08-16
  status: ready
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: docker.gitea.com/gitea:1.27.2
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: gitea
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THE INSTALL WIZARD IS OPEN TO THE FIRST VISITOR. Out of the box Gitea serves a setup page and its own docs tell you to open a browser to finish installing. On a public URL that means the first stranger to load it configures the instance AND creates the administrator. Worse than an unclaimed signup form, because the wizard also sets the database connection. Pass GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true so the wizard never renders, and create the admin yourself with the CLI (see the body). Verify it: GET / must NOT redirect to /install."
  - "⛔⛔ SET GITEA__security__SECRET_KEY. Verified in modules/setting/security.go: when SECRET_KEY is empty Gitea does NOT generate a random one, it falls back to a HARDCODED literal that is identical in every install that leaves it unset and is published in the open-source tree. It signs and encrypts stored secrets, including 2FA data and mirror credentials. Generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`, pass it as env, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy: changing it makes existing encrypted values undecryptable."
  - "GITEA__security__INTERNAL_TOKEN goes with the /data volume. If unset, Gitea generates one and writes it into app.ini inside /data. That is fine as long as /data is a real volume; if it is not, a redeploy invents a new token and internal API calls break. Either mount /data (which you must anyway, the repositories live there) or set the token explicitly."
  - "⛔ /data IS THE REPOSITORIES. Everything git lives on disk, not in Postgres: Postgres holds users, issues, pull requests and metadata, while the actual repository contents, the LFS objects, the avatars and app.ini are all under /data. A deploy without a persistent volume on /data loses every repository while the database still lists them. This is the single most important volume in the library."
  - "DATABASE: the override syntax is GITEA__section__KEY, so set GITEA__database__DB_TYPE=postgres, GITEA__database__HOST=\"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}\", GITEA__database__NAME=\"${PGDATABASE}\", GITEA__database__USER=\"${PGUSER}\", GITEA__database__PASSWD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Careful with both sides of that last one: Gitea's setting is spelled PASSWD while the value redu injects is PGPASSWORD, and GITEA__database__HOST takes host and port TOGETHER in one value rather than a separate port variable. Both are easy to get wrong and both fail as a connection error at boot. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself."
  - "PORT 3000 for HTTP. Pass 3000 to deploy_compose. The image also listens on 22 for git over SSH, which is NOT exposed by this deploy: see the SSH quirk."
  - "GIT OVER SSH IS NOT WIRED UP BY DEFAULT, AND THAT IS FINE. redu's public hostname terminates HTTPS, so `git clone https://<host>/user/repo.git` works immediately with a Gitea access token as the password. SSH clones need a TCP stream port, which is a separate piece of plumbing from the HTTPS hostname. Set GITEA__server__DISABLE_SSH=true and tell the user HTTPS is the clone path, rather than leaving a broken SSH URL displayed on every repository page. Do not promise SSH access you have not actually set up and tested."
  - "SET THE SERVER URLS: GITEA__server__ROOT_URL to the full https URL on the generated hostname, and GITEA__server__DOMAIN to the hostname. ROOT_URL is what Gitea prints in clone boxes, webhooks and emails, and it defaults to localhost, so leaving it unset gives every user a clone command that cannot work. Generate the dname yourself in the full `gitea-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "CLOSE REGISTRATION UNLESS THE USER WANTS IT OPEN. GITEA__service__DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. A public Gitea with open signup on a domain nobody is watching is a free file host, and that is a redu abuse problem as much as the user's. Ask, then set it deliberately either way."
  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email and no notification mail. Say so plainly; the admin password is the only way in until GITEA__mailer__* is wired to a provider the user owns."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Gitea creates and migrates its own schema at boot against an empty database."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 3000."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "SIZING: Gitea itself is a single Go binary and idles small, but git operations are memory hungry in bursts, because packing a large repository on clone or push happens in RAM. m1.medium is the sensible floor for anything with real repositories in it. Disk is the thing that actually runs out: repositories and LFS grow without limit, so size the volume with the user rather than defaulting."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. SECRET_KEY and the admin password belong to the user. Hand both over in the session; the deploy log records that the install was locked and an admin exists, never the values."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. Note the repositories live on the app VM's volume, so deleting the deployment DOES destroy the git data while the metadata database survives. Say that plainly before deleting anything."

# Self-host Gitea on redu

Your own git hosting: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Issues,
pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests.
- A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling
you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it
becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time.

**The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty
`SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it
unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default.

**The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files
under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and
has none of them.

## Proving the install is locked

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between
your Gitea and someone else's.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install.
final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")

case "$final" in
  *"/install"*)
    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked.
if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then
  echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2
fi

echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)."
echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."
```

Issues, pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU. ## What this deploys - **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000. - **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests. - A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live. - A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS. About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time. ## Deploy Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a directory containing this file: Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu. The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything. ## The three that actually break it **The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time. **The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty `SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default. **The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and has none of them. ## Proving the install is locked Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between your Gitea and someone else's. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public. # ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud set -eu HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh }" TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT # Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install. final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/") code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install") case "$final" in *"/install"*) echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2 echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2 echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2 exit 1 ;; esac # The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked. if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2 fi echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)." echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed." ``` ## Deploy log - Not yet deployed. Worse than an unclaimed signup form, because the wizard also sets the database connection. Pass GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true so the wizard never renders, and create the admin yourself with the CLI (see the body). Verify it: GET / must NOT redirect to /install." - "⛔⛔ SET GITEA__security__SECRET_KEY. Verified in modules/setting/security.go: when SECRET_KEY is empty Gitea does NOT generate a random one, it falls back to a HARDCODED literal that is identical in every install that leaves it unset and is published in the open-source tree. It signs and encrypts stored secrets, including 2FA data and mirror credentials. Generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`, pass it as env, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy: changing it makes existing encrypted values undecryptable." - "GITEA__security__INTERNAL_TOKEN goes with the /data volume. If unset, Gitea generates one and writes it into app.ini inside /data. That is fine as long as /data is a real volume; if it is not, a redeploy invents a new token and internal API calls break. Either mount /data (which you must anyway, the repositories live there) or set the token explicitly." - "⛔ /data IS THE REPOSITORIES. Everything git lives on disk, not in Postgres: Postgres holds users, issues, pull requests and metadata, while the actual repository contents, the LFS objects, the avatars and app.ini are all under /data. A deploy without a persistent volume on /data loses every repository while the database still lists them. This is the single most important volume in the library." - "DATABASE: the override syntax is GITEA__section__KEY, so set GITEA__database__DB_TYPE=postgres, GITEA__database__HOST=\"${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}\", GITEA__database__NAME=\"${PGDATABASE}\", GITEA__database__USER=\"${PGUSER}\", GITEA__database__PASSWD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Careful with both sides of that last one: Gitea's setting is spelled PASSWD while the value redu injects is PGPASSWORD, and GITEA__database__HOST takes host and port TOGETHER in one value rather than a separate port variable. Both are easy to get wrong and both fail as a connection error at boot. redu injects PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD into the project .env; deploy_compose never edits your compose, so interpolate them yourself." - "PORT 3000 for HTTP. Pass 3000 to deploy_compose. The image also listens on 22 for git over SSH, which is NOT exposed by this deploy: see the SSH quirk." - "GIT OVER SSH IS NOT WIRED UP BY DEFAULT, AND THAT IS FINE. redu's public hostname terminates HTTPS, so `git clone https:///user/repo.git` works immediately with a Gitea access token as the password. SSH clones need a TCP stream port, which is a separate piece of plumbing from the HTTPS hostname. Set GITEA__server__DISABLE_SSH=true and tell the user HTTPS is the clone path, rather than leaving a broken SSH URL displayed on every repository page. Do not promise SSH access you have not actually set up and tested." - "SET THE SERVER URLS: GITEA__server__ROOT_URL to the full https URL on the generated hostname, and GITEA__server__DOMAIN to the hostname. ROOT_URL is what Gitea prints in clone boxes, webhooks and emails, and it defaults to localhost, so leaving it unset gives every user a clone command that cannot work. Generate the dname yourself in the full `gitea-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match." - "CLOSE REGISTRATION UNLESS THE USER WANTS IT OPEN. GITEA__service__DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. A public Gitea with open signup on a domain nobody is watching is a free file host, and that is a redu abuse problem as much as the user's. Ask, then set it deliberately either way." - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so there is no password reset by email and no notification mail. Say so plainly; the admin password is the only way in until GITEA__mailer__* is wired to a provider the user owns." - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time. **The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. It is not a random per-instance default. **The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files under `/data`. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2 exit 1 ;; esac # The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked. if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then echo "WARN: /install answered 200. # Self-host Gitea on redu

Your own git hosting: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Issues,
pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests.
- A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling
you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it
becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time.

**The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty
`SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it
unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default.

**The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files
under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and
has none of them.

## Proving the install is locked

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between
your Gitea and someone else's.

> **Fixed 2026-08-16.** The earlier version of this script asked only "did `/` redirect to
> `/install`". A 502 from the edge proxy does not redirect, so it printed a green **OK** while
> Gitea was not running at all — and redu's hostname does answer with a 502 for a minute or two
> before the container comes up. It now requires a real 200 from Gitea itself before it will pass.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Follow redirects and record where we land AND what we got.
final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
root_code=$(curl -sSL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/")
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")

# GATE FIRST: a proxy error page does not redirect either, so without this check
# every assertion below passes against a Gitea that is not running.
if [ "$root_code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: / answered $root_code, not 200." >&2
  echo "Gitea is not serving yet (redu's edge answers 502 before the container is up)." >&2
  echo "Wait for status=ready and re-run. Do NOT treat this as locked." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -qi '<title>[^<]*Gitea' "$TMP/body"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: / returned 200 but the page is not Gitea." >&2
  exit 2
fi

case "$final" in
  *"/install"*)
    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# Once locked, Gitea does not register the wizard route at all: /install is 404.
# A 200 here means the lock did NOT apply.
if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: /install answered 200 — the wizard route is still registered." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: Gitea is serving (200), / does not redirect to the installer, /install is $code."
echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."
```

# Self-host Gitea on redu

Your own git hosting: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Issues,
pull requests, releases, a package registry and CI, on infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Gitea** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM for users, issues and pull requests.
- A volume on `/data`, which is where the repositories themselves live.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The install wizard.** Gitea ships serving a setup page, and its own documentation ends by telling
you to open a browser and finish installing. On a public URL the first stranger who loads it
becomes your administrator. Lock it at deploy time.

**The secret key.** This one is not the usual warning. Gitea's source shows that an empty
`SECRET_KEY` falls back to a **hardcoded literal**, the same one in every install that leaves it
unset, published in the open-source tree. It is not a random per-instance default.

**The data volume.** Postgres holds your issues and users. Your actual repositories are files
under `/data`. Without a volume there, a redeploy leaves a Gitea that lists every repository and
has none of them.

## Proving the install is locked

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It takes seconds and it is the difference between
your Gitea and someone else's.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Gitea is not serving its install wizard to the public.
#   ./verify-locked.sh gitea-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-locked.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Follow redirects and record where we land. An unlocked Gitea sends / to /install.
final=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{url_effective}' "https://$HOST/")
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/install")

case "$final" in
  *"/install"*)
    echo "FAIL: / redirects to $final" >&2
    echo "The install wizard is open. Anyone loading this URL can configure the instance" >&2
    echo "and create the administrator. Redeploy with GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK=true." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# The wizard route itself should not render a form once locked.
if [ "$code" = "200" ] && grep -qi 'install' "$TMP/body"; then
  echo "WARN: /install answered 200. Open it by hand and confirm it is not a setup form." >&2
fi

echo "OK: / does not redirect to the installer (landed on $final)."
echo "Now confirm your admin account signs in, and that registration is closed if you wanted it closed."
```

# Session report — deploying Gitea on redu, and tearing it down

**Date:** 2026-08-17 (deploy performed 2026-08-16 22:17–22:22 UTC)
**Operator account:** «REDACTED:env:013044ef»
**Working directory:** `/home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/gitea`
**Task:** *"Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu."* — followed by teardown at the end of the session.

---

## 1. Summary

at deploy time against the three failure modes `redu.md` warns about, verified by measurement
(not assumption), and then destroyed on request.

| | |
|---|---|
| Live URL (while it existed) | https://gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud |
| Deployment id | 423 |
| App VM | `b3bcd131-cbf6-4609-9299-18858bfb16fa` — m1.medium, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB |
| Managed Postgres | db #126, VM `db-gitea`, `[ip]:5432`, private-network only |
| Measured cost | **GBP 0.0452/hr (~GBP 33.00/mo)** — exactly the rate `redu.md` records |
| Time to ready | ~4 min (`deploy_compose` 22:17:55 → container up 22:21:53 UTC) |
| Final state | **Deployment destroyed** (see §7) |

---

## 2. What was read and planned

1. Read `redu.md` — a library file carrying 17 recorded quirks for this stack.
2. `whoami` — credential verified by real round-trip; quota headroom confirmed.
3. `check_deploy_prerequisites` — auto-selected `network_id f7102e8d-…` and keypair
   `redu-deploy-test`. Mode stayed **guided** (the user gave no YOLO signal).
4. Authored `docker-compose.yml` locally — one service, prebuilt image, no build step.

### The planner disagreed with the library, and the library won

`plan_deploy` auto-sized the app VM to **m1.large (GBP 0.066/hr)** because `needs_compose:true`
signals a stack that builds on the VM. This stack builds nothing — it runs a prebuilt image. The
planner surfaced the conflict itself as a `flavor-differs-from-record` preflight item.

Resolved in favour of `redu.md`'s recorded **m1.medium** by passing `flavor_id: "3"` explicitly.
`db_flavor_id: "2"` was also passed explicitly — omitting it defaults the DB VM to the app flavor
and roughly doubles that line of the bill.

**Effect: GBP 0.066/hr → GBP 0.0452/hr, a ~32% saving on the quoted rate.**

### Approval gate

The plan, the cost, and two open decisions were put to the user before anything billable was
created. The user chose: **registration closed**, **40 GB / m1.medium**, **deploy**.

---

## 3. Configuration applied

Env was passed to the compose project's `.env` for `${VAR}` interpolation; redu never edits the
compose file, so every value is interpolated explicitly in `docker-compose.yml`.

| Setting | Value | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK` | `true` | Out of the box the install wizard is open to the first visitor, who becomes the administrator **and** sets the DB connection. |
| `GITEA__security__SECRET_KEY` | generated, 32 random bytes (`openssl rand -hex 32`) | An empty key does **not** get randomised — Gitea falls back to a hardcoded literal published in its own open-source tree. |
| `GITEA__database__*` | `postgres`, `${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}`, name/user/`PASSWD` | Gitea spells it `PASSWD` while redu injects `PGPASSWORD`; host and port go together in one value. |
| `GITEA__server__ROOT_URL` / `DOMAIN` | the real hostname | Defaults to localhost, which breaks every clone box, webhook and email. |
| `GITEA__server__DISABLE_SSH` | `true` | No TCP stream port is wired up; advertising an SSH URL that cannot work is worse than not offering one. |
| `GITEA__service__DISABLE_REGISTRATION` | `true` | User's explicit choice. |
| `/data` volume | named volume `gitea-data` | **The repositories are files under `/data`.** Postgres holds only users, issues and PRs. |

`INTERNAL_TOKEN` was deliberately left unset — Gitea generates one and persists it into `app.ini`
on the `/data` volume, which is the documented-safe path when `/data` is a real volume.

No `migrate_command`: Gitea creates and migrates its own schema at boot against an empty database.

---

## 4. Deploy sequence

1. `prepare_upload` → tar + curl block. **Upload integrity checked**: local tarball 6592 bytes,
   server-recorded `size_bytes` 6592 — matched before the token was used.
2. `deploy_compose` — upload mode (`source_token`, no repo), `flavor_id "3"`,
   `database: managed`, `db_engine: postgres`, `db_flavor_id "2"`, port 3000,
   `dname: gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud`.
3. The `dname` was generated up front in the full `gitea-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it
   was known at deploy time and could be baked into `ROOT_URL`. redu used it **verbatim** — a bare
   label would have had a random suffix appended and would not have matched.
4. Polled to `status: ready`.

---

## 5. Verification — measured, not assumed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/version` | `{"version":"1.27.2"}` |
| `GET /` | 200, `<title>Gitea: Git with a cup of tea</title>`, no redirect to `/install` |
| `GET /install` | **404** — wizard route not registered |
| `GET /user/sign_up` | renders "Registration is disabled", zero input fields |
| `app.ini` `INSTALL_LOCK` | `true` |
| `app.ini` `SECRET_KEY` | literal string compare on the VM → **matches the generated 64-char key**, not the hardcoded fallback |
| `app.ini` `INTERNAL_TOKEN` | set, persisted on the `/data` volume |
| `app.ini` `ROOT_URL` / `DOMAIN` | `https://gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud/` / `gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud` |
| `app.ini` `DB_TYPE` / `HOST` | `postgres` / `[ip]:5432`, db `gitea`, user `gitea` |
| `app.ini` `DISABLE_SSH` | `true` |
| Admin auth (`GET /api/v1/user`) | 200, `login: milos`, `is_admin: true` |
| Wrong password | 401 |
| **Clone + push over HTTPS** | repo created via API, cloned with token, empty commit pushed, commit read back server-side |

The admin was created over the CLI:
`sudo docker exec -u git app-src-gitea-1 gitea admin user create --admin …`

The smoke-test repository and its access token were **deleted afterwards**; the instance was left
with 0 repositories.

---

## 6. Problems found and corrected

### 6.1 `verify-locked.sh` passed against a 502 — a security check that could not fail

The script shipped in `redu.md` asks only *"did `/` redirect to `/install`?"*. A proxy error page
does not redirect, so it printed a green **OK** while Gitea was not running at all.

This was not hypothetical: redu's public hostname answers with an openresty **502** for roughly
the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts. The script was run in that window and passed.
It was caught only by inspecting the response body — `<title>502 Bad Gateway</title>`.

**Fixed**: the script now requires HTTP **200** *and* Gitea's own `<title>` before any assertion is
evaluated, exiting `2 INCONCLUSIVE` otherwise. Verified against the live host (passes) and against
a non-Gitea 200 (correctly refuses). The corrected script is in `verify-locked.sh` and in the
`redu.md` body.

### 6.2 `/install` returns 404 when locked, not 200

The original script's `WARN if /install answered 200` branch can never fire on a correctly locked
instance — Gitea does not register the route at all. **404 is the positive signal**; a 200 there
means the lock did not apply. The check is now an outright FAIL on 200.

### 6.3 A false secret-key mismatch, self-inflicted

Comparing the key by hashing it on both sides produced a mismatch, because one side's `sha256sum`
input carried a trailing newline and the other's did not. Re-checked with a literal string compare
inside the container: **exact match, 64 chars**. Recorded in `redu.md` so the next run doesn't
repeat the scare — hash-comparison across a shell boundary invites a false alarm that looks
exactly like the hardcoded-fallback disaster.

### 6.4 Container name is not the service name

redu unpacks the upload into a compose project called `app-src`, so the container is
`app-src-gitea-1`. The host runs **docker**, not podman, as of this deploy. `-u git` is required or
Gitea complains about file ownership under `/data`.

---

## 7. Teardown

Performed at the user's explicit request at the end of the session.

> **Recorded outcome:** see §7.1 below.

### 7.1 Result

_(filled in immediately after the delete call — see the appended section at the end of this file)_

---

## 8. Files written

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docker-compose.yml` | One-service Gitea stack, all `GITEA__*` overrides interpolated from `.env`. |
| `redu.md` | Merged server-side via `get_deployment(redu_md:…)` so accumulated memory was preserved, then **6 new quirks added by hand** (redu's in-place merge explicitly does not write quirks) plus a full deploy-log entry. |
| `redu-deploy-plan.md` | Replaced the pre-deploy estimate with the real provisioned values, cost, and the verification table. |
| `verify-locked.sh` | The corrected verification script (§6.1). |
| `SESSION-REPORT.md` | This file. |

---

## 9. Notes for whoever runs this next

- **Pass the same `SECRET_KEY` on every redeploy.** Changing it makes existing encrypted values
  (2FA, mirror credentials) permanently undecryptable.
- **Pass the same `dname`** (`gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud`) to keep the URL stable.
- **No SMTP** on a default deploy: no password reset, no notification mail. The admin password is
  the only way in until `GITEA__mailer__*` is wired to a provider you own.
- **HTTPS is the clone path.** Use a Gitea access token as the password.
- **Disk is the constraint**, not CPU or RAM — 40 GB shared between OS and `/data`, and
  repositories plus LFS grow without limit.
- **Credentials are not in this file, or any file.** `redu.md` forbids committing them; the
  `SECRET_KEY` and admin password were handed to the user in-session only. They are moot now that
  the deployment is destroyed.

  billing.

# Session report — deploying Gitea on redu, and tearing it down

**Date:** 2026-08-17 (deploy performed 2026-08-16 22:17–22:22 UTC)
**Operator account:** «REDACTED:env:013044ef»
**Working directory:** `/home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/gitea`
**Task:** *"Read redu.md and deploy Gitea on redu."* — followed by teardown at the end of the session.

---

## 1. Summary

Gitea 1.27.2 was deployed to redu.cloud from a locally-authored one-service compose file, hardened
at deploy time against the three failure modes `redu.md` warns about, verified by measurement
(not assumption), and then destroyed on request.

| | |
|---|---|
| Live URL (while it existed) | https://gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud |
| Deployment id | 423 |
| App VM | `b3bcd131-cbf6-4609-9299-18858bfb16fa` — m1.medium, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB |
| Managed Postgres | db #126, VM `db-gitea`, `[ip]:5432`, private-network only |
| Measured cost | **GBP 0.0452/hr (~GBP 33.00/mo)** — exactly the rate `redu.md` records |
| Time to ready | ~4 min (`deploy_compose` 22:17:55 → container up 22:21:53 UTC) |
| Final state | **Deployment destroyed** (see §7) |

---

## 2. What was read and planned

1. Read `redu.md` — a library file carrying 17 recorded quirks for this stack.
2. `whoami` — credential verified by real round-trip; quota headroom confirmed.
3. `check_deploy_prerequisites` — auto-selected `network_id f7102e8d-…` and keypair
   `redu-deploy-test`. Mode stayed **guided** (the user gave no YOLO signal).
4. Authored `docker-compose.yml` locally — one service, prebuilt image, no build step.
5. `plan_deploy` with `redu.md` and the compose file pasted verbatim for server-side parsing.

### The planner disagreed with the library, and the library won

`plan_deploy` auto-sized the app VM to **m1.large (GBP 0.066/hr)** because `needs_compose:true`
signals a stack that builds on the VM. This stack builds nothing — it runs a prebuilt image. The
planner surfaced the conflict itself as a `flavor-differs-from-record` preflight item.

Resolved in favour of `redu.md`'s recorded **m1.medium** by passing `flavor_id: "3"` explicitly.
`db_flavor_id: "2"` was also passed explicitly — omitting it defaults the DB VM to the app flavor
and roughly doubles that line of the bill.

**Effect: GBP 0.066/hr → GBP 0.0452/hr, a ~32% saving on the quoted rate.**

### Approval gate

The plan, the cost, and two open decisions were put to the user before anything billable was
created. The user chose: **registration closed**, **40 GB / m1.medium**, **deploy**.

---

## 3. Configuration applied

Env was passed to the compose project's `.env` for `${VAR}` interpolation; redu never edits the
compose file, so every value is interpolated explicitly in `docker-compose.yml`.

| Setting | Value | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `GITEA__security__INSTALL_LOCK` | `true` | Out of the box the install wizard is open to the first visitor, who becomes the administrator **and** sets the DB connection. |
| `GITEA__security__SECRET_KEY` | generated, 32 random bytes (`openssl rand -hex 32`) | An empty key does **not** get randomised — Gitea falls back to a hardcoded literal published in its own open-source tree. |
| `GITEA__database__*` | `postgres`, `${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}`, name/user/`PASSWD` | Gitea spells it `PASSWD` while redu injects `PGPASSWORD`; host and port go together in one value. |
| `GITEA__server__ROOT_URL` / `DOMAIN` | the real hostname | Defaults to localhost, which breaks every clone box, webhook and email. |
| `GITEA__server__DISABLE_SSH` | `true` | No TCP stream port is wired up; advertising an SSH URL that cannot work is worse than not offering one. |
| `GITEA__service__DISABLE_REGISTRATION` | `true` | User's explicit choice. |
| `/data` volume | named volume `gitea-data` | **The repositories are files under `/data`.** Postgres holds only users, issues and PRs. |

`INTERNAL_TOKEN` was deliberately left unset — Gitea generates one and persists it into `app.ini`
on the `/data` volume, which is the documented-safe path when `/data` is a real volume.

No `migrate_command`: Gitea creates and migrates its own schema at boot against an empty database.

---

## 4. Deploy sequence

1. `prepare_upload` → tar + curl block. **Upload integrity checked**: local tarball 6592 bytes,
   server-recorded `size_bytes` 6592 — matched before the token was used.
2. `deploy_compose` — upload mode (`source_token`, no repo), `flavor_id "3"`,
   `database: managed`, `db_engine: postgres`, `db_flavor_id "2"`, port 3000,
   `dname: gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud`.
3. The `dname` was generated up front in the full `gitea-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so it
   was known at deploy time and could be baked into `ROOT_URL`. redu used it **verbatim** — a bare
   label would have had a random suffix appended and would not have matched.
4. Polled to `status: ready`.

---

## 5. Verification — measured, not assumed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/version` | `{"version":"1.27.2"}` |
| `GET /` | 200, `<title>Gitea: Git with a cup of tea</title>`, no redirect to `/install` |
| `GET /install` | **404** — wizard route not registered |
| `GET /user/sign_up` | renders "Registration is disabled", zero input fields |
| `app.ini` `INSTALL_LOCK` | `true` |
| `app.ini` `SECRET_KEY` | literal string compare on the VM → **matches the generated 64-char key**, not the hardcoded fallback |
| `app.ini` `INTERNAL_TOKEN` | set, persisted on the `/data` volume |
| `app.ini` `ROOT_URL` / `DOMAIN` | `https://gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud/` / `gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud` |
| `app.ini` `DB_TYPE` / `HOST` | `postgres` / `[ip]:5432`, db `gitea`, user `gitea` |
| `app.ini` `DISABLE_SSH` | `true` |
| Admin auth (`GET /api/v1/user`) | 200, `login: milos`, `is_admin: true` |
| Wrong password | 401 |
| **Clone + push over HTTPS** | repo created via API, cloned with token, empty commit pushed, commit read back server-side |

The admin was created over the CLI:
`sudo docker exec -u git app-src-gitea-1 gitea admin user create --admin …`

The smoke-test repository and its access token were **deleted afterwards**; the instance was left
with 0 repositories.

---

## 6. Problems found and corrected

### 6.1 `verify-locked.sh` passed against a 502 — a security check that could not fail

The script shipped in `redu.md` asks only *"did `/` redirect to `/install`?"*. A proxy error page
does not redirect, so it printed a green **OK** while Gitea was not running at all.

This was not hypothetical: redu's public hostname answers with an openresty **502** for roughly
the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts. The script was run in that window and passed.
It was caught only by inspecting the response body — `<title>502 Bad Gateway</title>`.

**Fixed**: the script now requires HTTP **200** *and* Gitea's own `<title>` before any assertion is
evaluated, exiting `2 INCONCLUSIVE` otherwise. Verified against the live host (passes) and against
a non-Gitea 200 (correctly refuses). The corrected script is in `verify-locked.sh` and in the
`redu.md` body.

### 6.2 `/install` returns 404 when locked, not 200

The original script's `WARN if /install answered 200` branch can never fire on a correctly locked
instance — Gitea does not register the route at all. **404 is the positive signal**; a 200 there
means the lock did not apply. The check is now an outright FAIL on 200.

### 6.3 A false secret-key mismatch, self-inflicted

Comparing the key by hashing it on both sides produced a mismatch, because one side's `sha256sum`
input carried a trailing newline and the other's did not. Re-checked with a literal string compare
inside the container: **exact match, 64 chars**. Recorded in `redu.md` so the next run doesn't
repeat the scare — hash-comparison across a shell boundary invites a false alarm that looks
exactly like the hardcoded-fallback disaster.

### 6.4 Container name is not the service name

redu unpacks the upload into a compose project called `app-src`, so the container is
`app-src-gitea-1`. The host runs **docker**, not podman, as of this deploy. `-u git` is required or
Gitea complains about file ownership under `/data`.

---

## 7. Teardown

Performed at the user's explicit request at the end of the session.

> **Recorded outcome:** see §7.1 below.

### 7.1 Result

_(filled in immediately after the delete call — see the appended section at the end of this file)_

---

## 8. Files written

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docker-compose.yml` | One-service Gitea stack, all `GITEA__*` overrides interpolated from `.env`. |
| `redu.md` | Merged server-side via `get_deployment(redu_md:…)` so accumulated memory was preserved, then **6 new quirks added by hand** (redu's in-place merge explicitly does not write quirks) plus a full deploy-log entry. |
| `redu-deploy-plan.md` | Replaced the pre-deploy estimate with the real provisioned values, cost, and the verification table. |
| `verify-locked.sh` | The corrected verification script (§6.1). |
| `SESSION-REPORT.md` | This file. |

---

## 9. Notes for whoever runs this next

- **Pass the same `SECRET_KEY` on every redeploy.** Changing it makes existing encrypted values
  (2FA, mirror credentials) permanently undecryptable.
- **Pass the same `dname`** (`gitea-duiaqt9c.redu.cloud`) to keep the URL stable.
- **No SMTP** on a default deploy: no password reset, no notification mail. The admin password is
  the only way in until `GITEA__mailer__*` is wired to a provider you own.
- **HTTPS is the clone path.** Use a Gitea access token as the password.
- **Disk is the constraint**, not CPU or RAM — 40 GB shared between OS and `/data`, and
  repositories plus LFS grow without limit.
- **Credentials are not in this file, or any file.** `redu.md` forbids committing them; the
  `SECRET_KEY` and admin password were handed to the user in-session only. They are moot now that
  the deployment is destroyed.
